clue.text: Visibly in agony showing talent with large drink

parts.note: a bent is a natural talent or aptitude
a double is a two-measure serving of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone's gift goes hand in hand with a big glass of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone folded over at the waist is plainly suffering, which is the idiom's sense of visible pain.

clue.text: Drink driving to here from here, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the words that come before are to be taken as spoken sounds

parts.note: in golf you drive from the tee towards the green, so the two places are green and tee

explanation.surface: A golfer wonders where to drive from and to.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf course lies behind 'driving': the drive goes from the tee to the green, and said aloud green tee is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is an unfermented tea, popular as a beverage.

clue.text: Grammatical construction comes apart at the seams, they say

indicators.note: they say marks the preceding words as a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: something that frays is unravelling at its edges

explanation.surface: A sentence falls to pieces, people report.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a group of words forming a unit within a sentence, a grammatical construction.

clue.text: Shakespeare's last words?

parts.note: the playwright's first name is also the document holding a person's final wishes, so Shakespeare's own testament is both

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the Bard said on his deathbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament sets out a person's final wishes, their last words in writing, and the Bard's forename is the same word.

clue.text: Fast spinner's cute finger work

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bowler's cunning finger action delivers quick turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast spinner' suggests a cricket bowler; it is a laboratory machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrifuge spins samples at high speed to separate their components.

clue.text: Film game with thousands instead of pennies

indicators.note: instead of says the remaining p in the game's name is also replaced by a k
with thousands means the game takes on a K in place of its first penny

parts.note: ping-pong is table tennis
p is the abbreviation for pennies
K stands for thousand, as in a salary of 30K

explanation.surface: A game where the stakes rise from pennies to thousands.
explanation.walkthrough: Ping-pong has two Ps; 'thousands instead of pennies' swaps each for a K.
explanation.definitionFit: King Kong is the 1933 monster film about a giant ape.

clue.text: Capital finds nothing given up after end of four months

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the month ending

parts.note: September to December all end in the same three letters

indicators.note: in a down answer, given up means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A city records zero gains after the year's last four months.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is the capital city of Germany.

clue.text: See 11
Listener and (briefly) The Telegraph given bit of a plug

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a wire is a telegram, sent by telegraph

explanation.surface: A Listener reader also glances at the Telegraph, with a power socket nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener and The Telegraph look like publications; they are an ear and a wire.
explanation.definitionFit: The earth wire is one of the three wires connected to a mains plug's pins.

clue.text: Old people arrested by police — nicked!

indicators.note: arrested by says the answer is held inside the following words

explanation.surface: Ancient Britons are caught by the cops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.

clue.text: 21 down's upper chamber given chop, accepted by ethical sort of lord

indicators.note: accepted by means the attic-and-chop pieces are taken inside the shuffled letters
sort of signals a kind of rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: a loft is the room at the top of a house
to hew is to chop with an axe

explanation.surface: Reforming the House of Lords: chop the upper chamber, says a principled peer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper chamber' suggests the House of Lords but is an attic; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London wrote the 1903 novel about a dog called Buck, so London's work is named via the cross-reference.

clue.text: Get gold switches supplied with wooden fasteners

indicators.note: switches here is a verb: the letters switch places

explanation.surface: Earn gold medals and swap things around.
explanation.definitionFit: Toggles are bar-shaped wooden fastenings, as on a duffel coat, so a toggled coat is fitted with them.

clue.text: See 11
Aristotle gets black eye restraining prisoner

indicators.note: restraining means holding the prisoner inside

parts.note: a shiner is a black eye
POW is prisoner of war

explanation.surface: The philosopher is punched while holding a captive.
explanation.walkthrough: Aristotle is not the philosopher but Aristotle Onassis, the Greek shipping magnate.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle Onassis built his fortune owning a merchant fleet of tankers, an example of the type.

clue.text: With us, night ban ludicrous, as this would be impossible!

definitions.text: With us, night ban ludicrous, as this would be impossible!

indicators.note: ludicrous signals the letters are thrown into a silly new order

explanation.surface: Banning the night would rule out a certain pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: With night banned it would always be day, so the whole clue is a joke: in fact you could do this all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in sunshine needs daylight, so the clue's mock-logic hides the opposite of the truth.

clue.text: Looked over again, seeing former dictator in grass

indicators.note: in places the former dictator inside the grass

parts.note: reed is a tall grass
ex means former
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: An ex-tyrant is spotted in the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect a second time is to look over again, a direct synonym.

clue.text: 7's food taken back, carried by English during appointment after breakfast, perhaps

indicators.note: after puts the remaining wordplay behind the cereal

parts.note: bran is a breakfast cereal, an example of breakfast

indicators.note: during means the English-and-food piece sits inside the appointment

parts.note: a date is an appointment

indicators.note: carried by means the reversed food is held inside the English abbreviation
taken back reads the food word in reverse

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: After breakfast, someone eats lunch on an English date.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is BERLIN, so '7's' points to a Berlin landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brandenburg Gate is Berlin's famous neoclassical monument, so the cross-reference reads as Berlin's landmark.

clue.text: Nearly desperate, walked round a country way

indicators.note: Nearly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: dire means desperate

indicators.note: round means the walking word goes around the a

parts.note: trod is past tense of tread, walked

explanation.surface: Nearly desperate, someone walked round a rural area.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirt road is an unpaved track, typical of the countryside.

clue.text: Sea air raised temperature separating acid compound

indicators.note: separating means the inner piece splits the shuffled acid
compound signals the letters are mixed together
in a down answer, raised means written upwards, so reversed

explanation.surface: Sea air raises the temperature of an acid compound.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is the sea between Italy and the Balkans.

clue.text: Remove drain endlessly taking cow dung into river

indicators.note: into puts the drained word and cow dung inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter

parts.note: to tire is to drain of energy
a cowpat is cow dung, so pat

explanation.surface: Someone clears a blocked drain by putting cowpats in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To extirpate is to root out or remove completely.

clue.text: 7's river rises in this? Quite the opposite

annotationWithheld.why: 7's river rises in this? Quite the opposite: def 7's (Irving Berlin's film Top Hat); 'river rises in this' seems PO reversed inside, but no parse found accounts for T and HAT or the 'Quite the opposite' twist
annotationWithheld.clue: 7's river rises in this? Quite the opposite

clue.text: Immature thing, 5, cradled by cricketer

indicators.note: cradled by means held inside the cricketer

parts.note: Brian Lara is the West Indian batting great
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A cricketer gently holds a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5 down but is just the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature stage of an insect, before metamorphosis.

clue.text: Capital putting lake above river

parts.note: on means above, resting on top of
the Don is a river in Russia and in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone places a lake upstream of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: London is the capital of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Little money left to invest in expression of derision

indicators.note: to invest in means to place something within, so left goes inside

parts.note: hah is a scornful exclamation
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A scornful sneer at a small sum to invest.
explanation.walkthrough: HA'PORTH is British slang for a halfpennyworth, a trivial amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfpennyworth is a tiny sum of money, as in 'a ha'porth of tar'.

clue.text: 21 down's suddenly murderous character to take on the traffic wardens?

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the violent alter ego of Dr Jekyll

parts.words: to take on the traffic wardens?
parts.note: to park is to leave a car where wardens may ticket it, provoking them

explanation.surface: A Jekyll-like figure fights traffic wardens in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is LONDON, so the answer is a London site; Hyde Park is a royal park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park is one of London's best-known royal parks, so the cross-reference reads as London's park.

clue.text: Tongue gets injection with iodine after joke

indicators.note: after places the injection and iodine behind the joke

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
a jab is an injection
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Someone gets an injection with iodine after a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi is a language spoken in Punjab in India and Pakistan; tongue means language.

clue.text: See 22
Article written after short play

indicators.note: written after places the article behind the short drink

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a dram
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece written after a brief play.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama is a play for performance on stage.

clue.text: Disastrous reactions to drug

indicators.note: Disastrous signals the letters going wrong and being rearranged

explanation.surface: Bad reactions to a medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To narcotise is to drug with a narcotic.
